submission.justification: Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage is recommended as it achieves the highest light collection (39.057 PE/MeV) among viable options. Module-D2, despite having better light yield, must be rejected due to exceeding the 5% failure rate limit after thermal cycling - a critical constraint since modules cannot be replaced once the cryostat is filled. Module-D3, while viable, provides substantially lower light collection (25.253 PE/MeV at 30% coverage). The 30% coverage maximizes light collection within the allowed range (5-30%), utilizing the scaling relationship (exponent 0.8) to achieve optimal photoelectron yield per MeV of deposited energy.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible light collection (photoelectrons per MeV)
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 at 30% coverage achieves 39.057 PE/MeV, which is the maximum among all viable configurations. Module-D3 at 30% only achieves 25.253 PE/MeV.

requirements.requirement: The module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 is one of the three candidate designs (D1, D2, D3) specified in the project documents.

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules may fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: Module-D1 is viable (Module_D1_viable = 1), meaning it meets the thermal cycling reliability requirement. Module-D2 was rejected (Module_D2_viable = 0) for exceeding this limit.
Recommended coverage is 30%, which is at the upper bound of the allowed range [5%, 30%].

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended module design and coverage
requirements.evidence: Submitting single recommendation: Module-D1 at 30% coverage.
